scheduled for the remainder of the full multi-year term.

risks.title: Severe Late Charges and Accelerated Administrative Fees
risks.original_clause:
Section 2. Fees, Invoicing, and Compounding Late Charges
All invoices are due immediately upon receipt. If Customer fails to remit payment within three (3) calendar days
of the invoice date, late interest shall accrue at 2.5% per month, compounded daily on the outstanding balance,
alongside a mandatory $500.00 administrative fee per delinquent notice.
risks.explanation: The payment window is unusually short, and late interest accrues at an elevated rate with daily compounding alongside per-notice penalty fees.
risks.why_it_matters: Even minor administrative delays in accounts payable could cause penalties and interest to compound rapidly into large sums.
risks.possible_consequences: Substantial unexpected financial liabilities accumulating quickly over routine invoicing disputes.
suggested_questions: Can the payment grace period be extended to a standard commercial 30-day window?
Can the late interest rate be capped at statutory rates without daily compounding?
risks.evidence_quote:
If Customer fails to remit payment within three (3) calendar days
of the invoice date, late interest shall accrue at 2.5% per month, compounded daily on the outstanding balance,
alongside a mandatory $500.00 administrative fee per delinquent notice.

risks.title: Unilateral Termination Rights and Acceleration of Future Fees
risks.original_clause:
Section 4. Unilateral Termination for Convenience
Vendor may terminate this Agreement at any time, with or without cause, immediately upon delivering electronic
notice to Customer. Customer shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience. In the event of
any early termination initiated by Customer, Customer shall immediately pay to Vendor all remaining fees
scheduled for the remainder of the full multi-year term.
risks.explanation: One party retains the asymmetrical right to cancel immediately without cause while demanding acceleration and payment of all future fees for the remaining contract term.
risks.why_it_matters: The counterparty can walk away from obligations while forcing you to pay for services you will not receive.
risks.possible_consequences: Immediate financial forfeiture and sudden disruption of operations without transition support.
suggested_questions: Can termination for convenience require 60 days advance written notice by either party?
Can fee acceleration clauses be removed so payments only cover services actually delivered?
risks.evidence_quote: Customer shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience.

risks.title: Uncapped and Unilateral Indemnification Obligation
risks.original_clause:
Section 5. Uncapped and Unlimited Indemnification
Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor, its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, and
contractors from and against any and all claims, liabilities, losses, damages, costs, and expenses (including
attorney's fees) arising out of or related to this Agreement without any limitation or financial cap whatsoever.
risks.explanation: This clause creates an open-ended, one-sided duty to indemnify and pay legal defense fees for the other party without an aggregate monetary limit.
risks.why_it_matters: You could be obligated to reimburse substantial third-party legal claims and attorney fees even if your fault was minimal.
risks.possible_consequences: Unquantifiable financial exposure and heavy litigation defense burdens arising from external lawsuits.
suggested_questions: Can this indemnification obligation be made mutual rather than unilateral?
Can an aggregate dollar cap equal to the annual fees paid under this agreement be added?

risks.title: Extreme Disproportion in Liability Limits and Warranty Disclaimers
risks.original_clause:
Section 6. Limitation of Vendor Liability
In no event shall Vendor's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement exceed one
hundred dollars ($100.00). Vendor disclaims all express and implied warranties, including merchantability,
fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement.
risks.explanation: The counterparty disclaims standard performance warranties while capping their maximum aggregate liability at a nominal dollar amount, offering minimal recourse if they breach.
risks.why_it_matters: If the counterparty causes substantial business disruption or data loss, your legal recovery could be capped at negligible sums.
risks.possible_consequences: Severe financial losses with virtually no avenue to recover damages from the defaulting vendor.
suggested_questions: Can the liability cap be increased to match 12 months of paid fees or the actual contract value?
Can exceptions for gross negligence, intentional misconduct, and confidentiality breaches be carved out?

risks.explanation: One party claims the unilateral right to alter agreement terms, pricing, or specifications at will without requiring mutual consent or advance notice.
risks.why_it_matters: The counterparty could increase pricing or diminish service commitments during the contract term without your approval.
risks.possible_consequences: Unexpected cost escalations and altered operational responsibilities with no contractual price protection.

Can a 60-day advance notice requirement with termination rights upon price changes be included?

This Agreement shall be effective for an initial term of two (2) years. Thereafter, this Agreement shall
automatically renew for successive terms of three (3) years each, unless Customer provides written notice of
non-renewal at least one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the expiration of the current term exclusively via

risks.explanation: The agreement renews automatically for multi-year commitments unless cancelled within an expansive advance notice window via restrictive delivery channels.

missing_provisions.clause_name: Detailed Scope of Work (SOW) and Acceptance Criteria
missing_provisions.why_it_matters: Vague deliverables without formal testing and acceptance procedures result in endless scope disputes and withheld payments.
missing_provisions.typical_provision: Services shall conform to the attached Statement of Work; client has 10 business days to inspect and notify defects.
missing_provisions.label: Possible omission

missing_provisions.clause_name: Intellectual Property Ownership and Client Deliverable Assignment
missing_provisions.why_it_matters: Ensures the paying client actually owns the custom deliverables and software code produced specifically for them.
missing_provisions.typical_provision: Client owns all custom deliverables upon full payment; vendor retains pre-existing tools and background IP.
missing_provisions.label: Possible omission

missing_provisions.clause_name: Service Level Agreement (SLA) and Uptime Commitment
missing_provisions.why_it_matters: Without an uptime guarantee and service credit remedy, clients have no recourse if cloud software suffers frequent outages.
missing_provisions.typical_provision: Vendor commits to 99.9% service availability, excluding scheduled maintenance, with service fee credits for downtime.
missing_provisions.label: Possible omission

missing_provisions.why_it_matters: Excuses performance delays caused by natural disasters, telecommunications outages, or government orders.
missing_provisions.typical_provision: Neither party is liable for performance delays caused by events beyond reasonable control.
missing_provisions.label: Possible omission
